$comment: The scorecard-local check: each file-based OpenSSF Scorecard check must score at least `floor` on the tracked tree (`scorecard --local`), and every `Warn:` finding must be listed in `accepted` (line number dropped). The keys are also the list of checks it runs. A local run raises a beaten floor and drops an accepted warning that's gone; adding an acceptance or lowering a floor loosens an allowlist and needs David's OK. Context: docs/tooling/ci.md § OpenSSF Scorecard.

accepted.reason: Gradle's wrapper jar, checked against Gradle's published checksums by gradle-wrapper.yml on every push. The public Scorecard sees that run and scores 10; local mode can't, hence 9 here.

accepted.warning: Warn: project license file does not contain an FSF or OSI license.
accepted.reason: Cmdr is BSL 1.1 on purpose (free for personal use), which isn't on the OSI list.

accepted.warning: Warn: containerImage not pinned by hash: apps/desktop/test/e2e-linux/docker/Dockerfile
accepted.reason: `FROM ${BASE_IMAGE}`: our own locally built E2E base, which has no registry digest. Folding it into Dockerfile.base as a stage would pin it, at the risk of the ~1 s entrypoint rebuild.

accepted.warning: Warn: npmCommand not pinned by hash: apps/website/Dockerfile
accepted.reason: `npm install --global pnpm@<exact>` in the website build. Pinning it alone doesn't move the score while the E2E image above stays, so it waits for that.

accepted.warning: Warn: no pull requests merged into dev branch
accepted.reason: Local mode has no PR history to read. The public check reads it, and workflows-hardening keeps CodeQL running on PRs.
The release jobs that create the GitHub release, upload assets, and push the website deploy commit. Job-scoped, as workflows-hardening requires; the score stays 10.
The caller of release-pipeline.yml has to grant what the reusable workflow's jobs ask for.

`e2e-base-image` pushes the E2E Docker base image to GHCR, only when the registry lacks the current tag. Test infra only (releases never use it), the token stays out of the Docker build, and fork PRs get a read-only token anyway. The jobs that only pull get `packages: read`; the score stays 10.

`prune-superseded-caches` deletes superseded `main` build caches after a land, so the repo stays under its 10 GB budget. Runs only on `main` pushes, with no checkout and no third-party action, just an inline `gh cache` script; `release.yml` can't be dispatched. The score stays 10.
